The AI race between the United States and China is getting closer, and China is no longer simply trying to catch up.

Chinese AI companies have produced powerful and increasingly affordable models, while open-weight systems from companies such as DeepSeek, Moonshot and Alibaba are putting pressure on US AI leaders. Stanford’s 2026 AI Index says the performance gap between US and Chinese frontier models has effectively closed, with the two countries repeatedly trading the lead.

China is also making progress beyond AI models. Its companies are developing domestic AI chips, expanding data-centre capacity and rapidly integrating AI into robotics and manufacturing. Recent reporting shows Chinese AI chipmakers are increasingly challenging Nvidia’s position in China.

But the US still has major advantages.

America has a huge lead in AI infrastructure, investment and data centres. Stanford reports that the US hosted 5,427 data centres, while US private AI investment reached $285.9 billion in 2025, compared with $12.4 billion in China.

So the question is no longer simply “Who has the better AI model?”

It is becoming a much bigger competition involving chips, computing power, data centres, investment, talent, robotics, software and global adoption.

And right now, the picture is surprisingly balanced: the US remains the infrastructure and investment leader, while China is rapidly closing the gap in AI models and gaining strength in open-weight AI and industrial applications.

The real AI superpower may ultimately be the country that can combine the best models + the most computing power + the strongest chips + the fastest real-world adoption.

node.text:
A million-token context window now costs zero dollars. Not a trial. Apache 2.0, on Qwen 4, weights any developer can download and ship inside a commercial product.

DeepSeek V4 Pro and Gemma 4.5 shipped 1M-class windows in the same stretch.

Mistral Voyage Pro landed at 512K and nobody blinked, which tells you where the bar sits now.

The door vendors were renting out by the token has come off its hinges.

Then an arXiv paper made the arithmetic strange.

1M-token inference on about 16GB of GPU RAM. The trick: attend to under 2% of the tokens and the model keeps over 95% of its performance while ignoring the rest. arXiv still renders tables like it's 1997, though the method section rewards the squint.

Sixteen gigabytes. One desktop card.

Any freight dispatcher could have explained this years ago.

A hub holding ten thousand packages does not open every box hunting one shipment; it pulls the manifests from the two trucks that matter and the package turns up before the coffee cools.

Same parcels. A fraction of the paperwork.

The old advice.

Stream a whole codebase into a hosted API and pay per token for the privilege — is now optional. Load a repository, or a few months of logs, into a local 1M-token window and run the retrieval questions until the answers hold up or fall apart. Cheaper, private, and the failure modes belong to the builder instead of a vendor's status page.

A DeepSeek acaba de fechar um pedido de 160 mil chips Huawei Ascend 950DT — o maior cluster da fabricante chinesa já registrado. O valor estimado da encomenda chega a US$ 2,56 bilhões, e a instalação será em um data center de 1 GW na Mongólia Interior.

O curioso é que a empresa sabe exatamente o que está abrindo mão: um chip NVIDIA GB300 equivale a quatro chips Huawei em poder de processamento. Mesmo assim, a DeepSeek seguiu em frente — e os motivos vão além da tecnologia.

A matéria completa no Hardware explica por que essa escolha pode ser mais estratégica do que parece, o que ela revela sobre o futuro da NVIDIA na China e onde estão os limites reais dos chips da Huawei. Deixe nos comentários o que você acha dessa disputa.

#DeepSeek #Huawei #NVIDIA #Inteligência Artificial #Semicondutores

Chinese AI does not have to be fully trusted for its technology to be taken seriously. Models from companies such as DeepSeek and Qwen are becoming increasingly competitive, often offering strong performance at lower costs and with open-weight access. That is forcing businesses and governments to judge Chinese AI on performance.

The bigger issue is whether users can manage the risks while benefiting from rapid innovation. Concerns over data, censorship, intellectual property and possible US-China technology restrictions remain, but open models can also be independently tested and adapted.

2 horas de conferência manual. 5 minutos com DeepSeek. O que muda é o pedido.

O erro mais comum é pedir 'faça um memorial'. Isso devolve texto genérico. O truque é ser específico: pedir áreas, materiais, volumes. O DeepSeek raciocina com custo baixo e faz a conta certa.

Exemplo: em vez de 'Faça um memorial', escreva 'A partir da planta, extraia a área de cada cômodo, liste os materiais de acabamento e calcule o volume de concreto da laje em m³.' O resultado sai direto.

Como aplicar hoje:
Abre o DeepSeek agora e cole a sua planta. Peça: 'Extraia áreas de cada cômodo e liste materiais de acabamento.' Confira se os números batem.

Qual desses dois pedidos você já usou? O genérico ou o específico? Responde aqui embaixo.

PREÇOS EM UM QUARTO DE SEU NÍVEL ORIGINAL 

A startup chinesa de inteligência artificial DeepSeek anunciou um corte permanente de 75% nos preços do modelo V4-Pro, principal sistema da empresa voltado para IA generativa.

Com a mudança, os custos da API passaram de até 24 iuanes para até 6 iuanes (cerca de US$0,0035 a US$0,83) por milhão de tokens, unidade usada para processar textos em modelos de inteligência artificial.

A empresa não confirmou se a redução está ligada ao aumento da oferta dos chips Ascend 950, da Huawei, usados no treinamento e operação do V4-Pro.

O movimento acontece em meio ao avanço das fabricantes chinesas de chips, beneficiadas pelas restrições impostas pelos Estados Unidos à venda de semicondutores avançados da Nvidia para a China.

Behörden und Cybersicherheitsfachleute haben gravierende Sicherheitsbedenken gegen den chinesischen KI-Chatbot DeepSeek. Ein wesentlicher Kritikpunkt ist die Speicherung der Tastatureingaben. 

DeepSeek informiert in seinen Datenschutzhinweisen darüber, dass „Tastatureingabemuster oder -rhythmen“ erfasst werden – ein Verfahren, das zur Identifizierung von Nutzer:innen eingesetzt werden kann. „Auch Tastatureingaben innerhalb der App können womöglich mitgelesen werden, bevor sie abgeschickt werden“, sagt eine Sprecherin des Bundesamts für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI) auf dpa-Anfrage. 

Abgesehen davon ist DeepSeek nach chinesischem Recht verpflichtet, sämtliche Daten in der Volksrepublik zu speichern. Das chinesische Geheimdienstgesetz wiederum verpflichtet Bevölkerung und Organisationen zur Kooperation mit den Sicherheitsbehörden. Der Gummiparagraf wird von etlichen China-Beobachter:innen als Zugriffsrecht des Spionageapparats auf sämtliche in der Volksrepublik gespeicherten Daten interpretiert. 

Die etablierte US-Konkurrenz von Open AI hingegen sichert zu, nicht aktiv nach persönlichen Daten zu suchen und keine öffentlichen Daten im Internet zum Aufbau persönlicher Profile zu verwenden. Allerdings gibt es auch ein US-Gesetz – den Cloud Act – das amerikanische Firmen verpflichtet, den Behörden Zugriff auf im Ausland gespeicherte Daten zu gewähren. 

Derzeit bereitet der Datenschutzbeauftragte von Rheinland-Pfalz ein Prüfverfahren gegen DeepSeek vor. „Mehrere deutsche Datenschutzaufsichtsbehörden gehen voraussichtlich parallel vor“, sagte eine Sprecherin auf Anfrage. Laut EU-Datenschutzgrundverordnung muss ein Unternehmen ohne Niederlassung in der EU zumindest einen gesetzlichen Vertreter benennen, was DeepSeek bislang offenbar nicht getan hat.

China is tightening control over its booming artificial intelligence sector, not just through technology but also by restricting the movement of the people building it. According to reports, Chinese authorities are now limiting overseas travel for top AI researchers, startup founders and executives working at companies like Alibaba and DeepSeek amid growing fears over foreign influence and national security risks.

The move comes after China reportedly blocked Meta from acquiring AI startup Manus AI and reflects Beijing’s escalating focus on winning the global AI race against the United States. Experts say the rivalry is no longer only about chips and software but also about controlling talent, expertise and access to cutting-edge innovation.

Rival do ChatGPT 📲 "A forma como eles fizeram foi totalmente diferente da maioria das empresas de tecnologia", diz Cleber Zanchettin, professor do Centro de Informática da Universidade Federal de Pernambuco (CIn-UFPE), montado na década de 1980 e hoje um dos líderes em pesquisa em inteligência artificial na América Latina.⁠
⁠
O chatbot de inteligência artificial chinês DeepSeek-R1 foi lançado discretamente em 20 de janeiro de 2025.⁠
⁠
À medida que os especialistas foram testando o modelo e entendendo como tinha sido construído, perceberam que de fato rivalizava com os das big techs americanas — e embaralhava a disputa entre EUA e China pelo posto de superpotência da tecnologia.⁠
⁠
Uma semana depois, o Vale do Silício entrou em pânico. As ações das 7 principais empresas de tecnologia dos Estados Unidos desidrataram e as Magnificent 7 (Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet (Google), Amazon, Nvidia, Tesla e Meta) perderam US$ 1 trilhão em valor de mercado em 27 de janeiro.⁠
⁠
Mas, para além da alta tensão na arena dos negócios e da geopolítica, a inovação em si trazida pela plataforma impressionou a comunidade científica, ressalta Zanchettin.⁠
⁠
Em entrevista à BBC News Brasil, o especialista mergulhou em quatro características que explicam porque o DeepSeek impressionou.⁠
⁠
A análise completa você encontra no nosso link da bio: @BBCBrasil⁠

No início do ano, a startup chinesa surpreendeu os mercados de tecnologia com seu modelo de IA de código aberto e acirrar a disputa com a OpenAI.

A fabricante chinesa ainda afirmou que vai habilitar recursos avançados de assistência ao motorista em quase todos os seus futuros modelos sem custo adicional para os compradores. 

Uma das medidas será colocar o sistema de assistência ao motorista, chamado God’s Eye, em veículos com preços a partir de 100.000 yuan (US$ 13.688) na China e o incluirá em vários modelos de menor custo, como o popular hatchback Seagull.

China is making waves in technology with its underwater data center, a groundbreaking move that could transform cloud computing and data storage. By placing data centers beneath the ocean, China aims to tackle major challenges in energy consumption, land usage, and environmental impact.

One of the biggest advantages is natural cooling. Traditional data centers require massive amounts of electricity to prevent overheating, but underwater facilities use the cold ocean water to keep servers at optimal temperatures. This can reduce energy consumption and cut operational costs significantly.

Additionally, underwater data centers free up valuable land space, making them a practical solution for densely populated cities. Since they are submerged near coastal areas, they can also enhance data transfer speeds for users in nearby urban hubs, reducing latency and improving efficiency.

Beyond efficiency, this innovation is a step toward sustainability. With lower power consumption and a reduced carbon footprint, underwater data centers align with global efforts to create greener technology solutions. China’s move follows previous experiments, like Microsoft’s Project Natick, but on a larger scale, signaling potential mainstream adoption in the future.

If successful, China’s underwater data center could set a new industry standard, reshaping how the world stores and processes data. This futuristic approach might soon become the norm, paving the way for a more efficient, sustainable, and high-performance cloud computing era.
